readme.purpose: Ground-truth fixture for the PBT 3D explainer. Every key/hash/chunk was produced by the real EIP-8297 reference implementation (execution-specs-ports-wt, src/ethereum/binary_trie/{trie.py,embedding.py}), never hand-typed.

world_snapshots.W0: WB + MegaToken deployed with full initial supply to the deployer (=post-J2)
world_snapshots.W1: W0 + ERC-20 distributed to 4 holders + VaultTemplate#1 receives a deposit; the shared pre-state for most journeys and for the top-level node/leaf list below

readme.top_level_nodes_leaves: computed on W1; node.id is the first 14 hex chars of that node's own real merkleize() hash
readme.journeys: each has pre_state (a world snapshot id, or 'W1+J4a' meaning W1 after J4a's writes), pre_root/post_root, derivation_steps (label/formula/inputs/output using real computed values), writes (key/before/after/action), hashes_recomputed ({branches_recomputed, leaves_changed} -- branches_recomputed is the union of root-to-changed-leaf branch positions in the post-tree, see compute_recompute_stats)
readme.zone_atlas: computed from W1: root_split confirms which side bit0=0/1 lands on; leaf_counts_by_zone; megatoken_storage_groups counts distinct (zone||key_hash(addr)||key_hash(addr||tree_index)) prefixes actually populated
readme.why_pbt: W1-W9; W1/W2/W6/W7/W9 numbers are EIP-8297 text figures (Motivation/Rationale/Security Considerations), W3/W4/W5/W8 are computed from this fixture
readme.hash_function: BLAKE3 for tree merkleization and key_hash (EIP-8297, explicitly not final); Keccak256 for code_hash/EXTCODEHASH/CREATE addresses/Solidity mapping-and-array slot derivation (unaffected by PBT's hash choice, EIP-8297 Backwards Compatibility)

journeys.title: Send ETH to a brand-new address
journeys.teaches: Absence -> insertion split; a plain value transfer creates two brand-new 2-leaf EOAs (recipient + coinbase) while the sender's existing BASIC_DATA leaf is merely updated.

derivation_steps.label: recipient address padding
recipient header stem
recipient BASIC_DATA key
recipient CODE_HASH key (EOA: keccak(""))
fee recipient (coinbase) header stem, same formula, new address
balance arithmetic (EVM/EIP-1559 economics, not a tree formula)
derivation_steps.formula: sender_after = sender_before - value - gas_used*(base_fee+priority_fee); coinbase += gas_used*priority_fee; base_fee portion is burned (credited nowhere)

journeys.title: Deploy a contract (from scratch)
journeys.teaches: Full code-zone merkleization walk for a brand-new code_hash: chunking, 2 code groups (>256 chunks), header creation, constructor writes split across header slots and the storage zone.

derivation_steps.label: CREATE address (already computed off-chain, cast compute-address)
code_hash
chunkify_code
code chunk 0 key (first code group)
code chunk 256 key (second code group, tree_index=1)
header creation
constructor storage: totalSupply (header slot, slot 2 < 64)
constructor storage: owner (header slot, slot 3 < 64, packed with paused)
constructor storage: balanceOf[deployer] (Solidity mapping, storage zone since slot>=64)
derivation_steps.formula: storage_key = keccak256(pad32(deployer) || pad32(4)); key = 0xFF || key_hash(addr32) || key_hash(addr32||tree_index) || sub

journeys.title: Deploy the same bytecode again (dedup)
journeys.teaches: Second and third deployments of identical bytecode write zero new code-zone leaves; content-addressing means only a new 34-byte header stem is created per deployment.

derivation_steps.label: CREATE address for 3rd deployment
code_hash is IDENTICAL to VaultTemplate #1 and #2
derivation_steps.formula: code_hash = keccak256(runtime_code); same runtime_code bytes as the first 2 deployments

derivation_steps.label: code chunk keys are therefore IDENTICAL too -> no new code-zone leaves
derivation_steps.formula: get_tree_key_for_code_chunk(code_hash, i) depends only on code_hash and i, never on the deploying address

derivation_steps.label: only a new header is created for the new address
derivation_steps.formula: BASIC_DATA + CODE_HASH leaves at the new address's own stem

journeys.title: Delegate an EOA (EIP-7702)
journeys.teaches: sub2 written, sub1 removed, code_size=23; a dashed resolves-to link (not a tree edge) points at the target's own CODE_HASH leaf.

derivation_steps.label: delegation indicator
DELEGATION_LEAF_KEY
delegation value (padded to 32B)
CODE_HASH leaf removed
derivation_steps.formula: embed_account unconditionally clears CODE_HASH when is_delegation(code)

derivation_steps.label: nonce bump (EIP-7702 protocol rule, not EIP-8297)
derivation_steps.formula: authorizing account's nonce += 1 per used authorization

derivation_steps.label: resolves-to: target's own header/code (weak link, not a tree edge)
derivation_steps.formula: target's CODE_HASH leaf and code group are looked up by client software following the 20-byte target, never a stored tree pointer

journeys.title: Re-delegate to a new target
journeys.teaches: Same DELEGATION_LEAF_KEY leaf, value overwritten; the resolves-to link now points at a different code group.

derivation_steps.label: delegation value overwritten in place (same DELEGATION_LEAF_KEY)

journeys.title: Revoke a delegation (authorize to 0x0)
journeys.teaches: Delegation leaf removed; CODE_HASH leaf restored to keccak("") with code_size zeroed, exactly the shape of a never-delegated EOA.

derivation_steps.label: authorization to the zero address clears delegation
derivation_steps.formula: code=b"" -> is_delegation(code) is False -> DELEGATION_LEAF_KEY removed, CODE_HASH leaf restored to keccak("")

journeys.title: Transfer an ERC-20
journeys.teaches: Mapping-slot derivation (Solidity, Keccak) feeds the EIP-8297 storage-zone key formula (BLAKE3); sender update + recipient insert in two different storage groups of the same bucket; contrast with a header slot.

derivation_steps.label: sender balance slot (mapping, Solidity convention)
sender storage-zone key
recipient balance slot (fresh insert)
contrast: MegaToken's OWN totalSupply is a header slot (slot 2 < 64), unaffected by a transfer
derivation_steps.formula: get_tree_key_for_storage_slot(mega32, 2) resolves to the header stem, not the storage zone

journeys.title: Call a contract (partial code witness)
journeys.teaches: Only the chunks execution actually visits are needed in a witness; a call to transfer(address,uint256) touches the dispatcher chunks plus the function-body chunk starting at its real JUMPDEST, not all 263 chunks of MegaToken.

derivation_steps.label: function selector
dispatcher JUMPDEST for this selector (found by disassembling the real runtime bytecode)
derivation_steps.formula: scan PUSH4<selector> ... PUSH2<dest> ... JUMPI in the compiled dispatcher

derivation_steps.label: dispatcher chunks (every call touches these first)
PUSHDATA jumpdest-validity byte reused for witness/EVM alike
derivation_steps.formula: chunk byte0 = leading PUSHDATA run length also tells the EVM whether the JUMPDEST at this offset is real code or mid-operand data

output.note: same byte0 field serves chunking and jumpdest-analysis

notes: Companion to J5; touches the same account, writes nothing new -- see J5 for the storage-zone mutation this call would also perform.

journeys.title: Clear a slot (write zero)
journeys.teaches: A write of 32 zero bytes resolves to a deletion at the state layer; the tree's own one-level merge (surviving sibling promoted, prefix spliced if it's a branch) restores canonical form.

derivation_steps.label: withdraw(1 ether): balance storage var -> 0
derivation_steps.formula: state_write collapses a 32-zero-byte write to a deletion

derivation_steps.label: header sub-index of slot 1

journeys.title: Deploy a big contract (>256 chunks)
journeys.teaches: A contract past 256 chunks spans 2+ code groups scattered across the code zone (each keyed by key_hash(code_hash||tree_index), unrelated stems); a PUSH32 operand can straddle a chunk boundary; a genuine zero-code, non-PUSHDATA run is an absent chunk.

derivation_steps.label: chunk count
code groups
derivation_steps.formula: tree_index = chunk_id // 256; group 0 = chunks 0-255, group 1 = chunks 256+

derivation_steps.label: genuine all-zero absent chunk
derivation_steps.formula: chunk encodes to 32 zero bytes (zero code AND byte0=0) -> absent, from RESERVED_ZERO_REGION

derivation_steps.label: PUSH32 straddling a chunk boundary
derivation_steps.formula: opcode 0x7F operand is 32 bytes > 31-byte chunk width

notes: Same deployment as J2; this beat is a detail lens on its code-zone layout, not a separate write.

journeys.title: Prove it (witness anatomy)
journeys.teaches: A PBT witness is the path plus exactly one sibling hash per level (arity 2); shown against MPT's 15-wide branches at the same real depth.

derivation_steps.label: presence witness: Acct4's MegaToken balance leaf
derivation_steps.formula: per level: encode_bit_prefix(this branch) + sibling hash

derivation_steps.label: absence witness: Acct1's BASIC_DATA key (Acct1 does not exist in W1)
derivation_steps.formula: walk diverges at the first bit where the key differs from the tree; terminal neighbor leaf's full key+value proves the divergence

derivation_steps.label: MPT comparison (EIP-8297 Motivation, exact quoted figure)
derivation_steps.formula: 15 siblings * 32 bytes * 12 levels (typical MPT account-trie depth)

journeys.title: One block, many writes
journeys.teaches: Independent writes across zones/accounts (J1's ETH send, J5's ERC-20 transfer, J4a's delegation) share upper branch nodes; one bottom-up recomputation recomputes the union, not the naive per-write sum.

derivation_steps.label: combined write set
derivation_steps.formula: union of J1 + J5 + J4a's individual key/value changes applied to one trie

derivation_steps.label: branch recompute: union vs naive sum
derivation_steps.formula: branches_recomputed(union) <= branches_recomputed(J1)+branches_recomputed(J5)+branches_recomputed(J4a); equality only if the three write sets share no ancestor

notes: Naive per-journey sum would be 32 branch recomputes; the real single bottom-up pass recomputes 27 because paths meet near the root (EIP-8297 Rationale, "Single tree with zones").

journeys.title: SELFDESTRUCT in creating tx (shared code)
journeys.teaches: Header and storage leaves are removed unconditionally; code chunks survive because 3 sibling VaultTemplate instances still share the same code_hash -- the account leaves no trace, but the code stays exactly because other accounts still reference it.

derivation_steps.label: deploy: code_hash identical to 3 existing siblings -> chunk writes are no-ops (same as J3)
new header created at VaultTemplate#4's own address
SELFDESTRUCT in creating tx (EIP-6780): header + storage removed unconditionally
code_hash still referenced by 3 other live accounts -> code chunks NOT removed
derivation_steps.formula: reference check: does any account in the resulting state have this code_hash?

notes: post_root == pre_root (True): created-and-destroyed in one tx leaves zero trace in the committed state (EIP-6780).

journeys.title: SELFDESTRUCT in creating tx (unique code)
journeys.teaches: Contrast with J11a: this contract's bytecode is unique, so its code-zone leaves are written on create AND removed on destroy, not just header/storage -- both variants still leave zero net trace in the committed root.

derivation_steps.label: deploy: brand-new unique code_hash -> new code chunks written
SELFDESTRUCT in creating tx: header + storage removed unconditionally
code_hash referenced by no other account -> code chunks ARE removed
derivation_steps.formula: reference check against the resulting state finds zero holders

notes: post_root == pre_root (True): created-and-destroyed in one tx leaves zero trace in the committed state (EIP-6780).
